希望有人能把老版本的汉化移植到steam版上，steam版的2003性能比日版的要强上许多，而且有人做了拓展补丁使之性能进一步的提升，甚至支持导入插件。
让我想使用这个老到掉牙的引擎的原因是因为接触了日本的一个叫VIPRPG的亚文化系列，这个系列有不少作品都让我见识到了rpgmaker200x的性能是多么的恐怖，从而让我自己也萌生了用这个引擎做一些作品的念头。至于为什么是2003不是2000，除了开头提到的原因以外，还有2003本身也是2000的加强版，2000能做到的2003同样也能做到甚至能做得更好。
这个引擎本身也有一些可以说道的地方，比如这一作的默认素材是个人认为是整个系列里最好看最好听的，强推战斗3，简直神曲，默认的素材量也是完全足够做出一个小品级的rpg游戏。还有预设支持2x、4x和8x的显示比例，画地图相对后续几作要直观一些。自带atb回合制等等。
不过如果是抱着我想用这个做游戏赚钱的心态的话，个人还是更推荐后面几作一些，毕竟迭代了这么多次，后续的引擎肯定是要比这个引擎要好用的，而且后续的几作原生支持导入插件，甚至还自带加密功能。此外2003本身的局限也挺大，比如默认情况下导入的素材不能超过8位256色，超过的得手动降素材的彩度，还有一张地图的元件图片只能指定一张图之类的。

The best RPG Maker and the best side-view battle system yet. I had THOUSANDS AND THOUSANDS of hours messing with RPGM2K3 as a kid when my dad first bought a CD who contained the software... I loved creating short games with Final Fantasy-ish lore back then, but most times I ran it only to spend an unholy amount of time just fighting custom crazy godlike bosses with random heroes created on the fly.

Every other RPG Maker is a downgrade to this one in almost every way, except for plugin support and tilesets. Because RPGM2K3 is so limited in terms of map design (and this issue was finally completely solved only in MV and beyond), it forces you to meticulously craft your complex scenes using parallax on external softwares (also how I started learning Photoshop and pixel art) instead of actual tileset building  - that should be reserved to interactables and "front row" stuff.

Absolutely recommended if you want a retrolike RPG with the most solid side view battle out there that demands no absurd plugins to be fun or look cool. Parallaxes may be scary at first, but there's a lot more freedom in setting up worlds outside grids and once you get used to it, you never wanna go back to that primitive native map designer. You can already do too much with events - I'd say on par with today's RPG Makers with some tinkering. It also features the most beautifully drawn battlers between all RTPs, which is a damn huge plus.

RPG Maker 2003 is the holy grail of retrolike makers.

in general rpg maker 2003 is great for unorthodox art styles, many strange games have been made with it
i like how you don't even have to use plugins or whatever you can just come up with a solution with the tools provided

that cuts down on time significantly for me because i like screwing around with limitations like that
plus honestly this engine lacks the capability of your game feeling like some fake pixel art stuff since you actually deal with limitations that naturally make your art style compatible with a snes/ds-like feel

in general the simplicity is very welcome, i feel the modern rpg makers lose that aspect

though one thing i will say is that maniax patch makes this engine so much better since it gives a lot more options
it doesn't fix some main issues though like uhhhh

there's a problem when you shut down your computer or crash with rpg maker 2003 open, the game engine decides "screw you" and makes its so your project's file tree corrupts
you can fix this by opening a new project and putting the same amount of maps as the old file tree, then copying that project's file tree (the .lmt file in the project folder) to your old project, but you'll have to rename the maps back, plus you'll need to redo map properties if you've done any of that

you can also use an exe on the internet to fix it by using it in the project folder but that does not work on maniax patch

i think the battle system this engine uses is interesting even if most people wouldn't want it
it's basically like final fantasy's snes games with the atb system, it's interesting

speed matters a lot since it's sort of real time with turns
i think it's pretty good if you were to use it properly, games like OFF definitely weren't the best examples i think

i wish there was an option to use 2k's battle system if you wanted, but i do like the side battlers
it would've been better if you could decide to use atb or not and decide to use side battle or not as well

there is plenty of advice/tutorials with rpg maker 2003 on the internet though if you're ever stuck, so it's actually not bad in terms of learning the engine, though if you encounter a niche problem you might have some trouble

if you're looking to do text blip stuff for example, maniax patch would have to be where you'd go
maniax patch isn't very easy to understand either, you have to tinker with it a bit

this engine only supports mp3/midi for music as well unless you use the maniax patch which i think supports ogg

i wish this engine had more updates to fix problems like the ones outlined above
maybe they could've added a way for text blips in base rpg maker 2003 to not be so cumbersome to do

but overall, it's a great engine and really simple to use, i just wish it was better in some aspects
